change.repo: the iCalendar (RFC 5545) export library of a privacy-focused open-source calendar app (pure-JVM Kotlin module)
change.diff_range: S0..S1 (the generator: CR normalization in the TEXT escaper + routing VALARM text fields through it)

claims.claim: Emitted iCalendar TEXT values are RFC 5545-clean: a lone/CRLF carriage return in an event DESCRIPTION is normalized to an escaped newline (no bare CR survives), and VALARM DESCRIPTION/SUMMARY/RELATED-TO have their commas, semicolons, and backslashes escaped.

surface.transport: public generate() API -> emitted VCALENDAR string
surface.how_reached: compiled the module at S0 and S1, called the public generator through its package boundary with adversarial input, captured the emitted bytes

claims.how_established: Built the calendar export module at S0 and S1 in isolated detached git worktrees (working repo untouched), compiling main sources directly with the cached Kotlin compiler + ical4j classpath (no Android SDK, no app, no network). Drove the PUBLIC generate() API (not the private escaper) with an event whose DESCRIPTION carries a CRLF and a lone CR, plus a DISPLAY VALARM whose text fields carry comma/semicolon/backslash. Captured the emitted VCALENDAR string at both commits. The only non-deterministic fields (DTSTAMP time, generated UIDs) were normalized to «redacted» IDENTICALLY in both captures, so the artifact diff is exactly the fix; the byte-level properties under test (lone-CR count; escaping of the three VALARM TEXT lines) are preserved verbatim.

artifacts.summary: S0: DESCRIPTION contains 2 bare CRs; VALARM text emitted raw (unescaped comma/semicolon/backslash)
S1: 0 bare CRs (all normalized to \n); VALARM text fully escaped

differential.probe: generate(event with DESCRIPTION 'line one\r\nline two\rline three' + DISPLAY VALARM with comma/semicolon/backslash in its text)
differential.s0_observed: DESCRIPTION has 2 lone CRs; VALARM DESCRIPTION/SUMMARY/RELATED-TO unescaped
differential.observed_delta: bare-CR count 2 -> 0 in DESCRIPTION; three VALARM TEXT properties now escaped

gaps.desc: The REAL end-user surface is the app's 'Export / Share .ics' action in the Android GUI; only the library boundary (the generator's public API) was driven. The wiring from the export button through to the generator was not exercised, so a defect BETWEEN the GUI and this library (wrong event assembled, export not invoked, file not shared) would not be caught here.
gaps.why_unverified: no Android emulator/device in this environment and the app is read-only; driving the GUI export flow is out of scope. The right rung for the GUI surface is undriven (rung 0).

gaps.desc: One representative adversarial input was driven. RFC 5545 TEXT has other edge cases (e.g. a trailing backslash, mixed CR/LF ordering, non-ASCII adjacent to escapes) not each exercised at the surface.
gaps.why_unverified: one input covers the changed branch; exhaustive TEXT-grammar fuzzing was out of the timebox
